facts.text: Moline sits on a slightly elevated plateau in Wildcat Creek valley, named by Native Americans for the bobcats that roamed the stream.
In 1904, Moline built Kansas' oldest swinging bridge, a suspension-type bridge that still spans Wildcat Creek today.
A limestone waterfall on an intermittent stream lies just west of the famous Swinging Bridge, adding a natural landmark to the town.
The annual Saturday morning parade features local law enforcement, fire fighters, cowboys, tractors, and unique floats, with candy tossed to children along Main Street.
Shaffer House Museum and Art Center, at the corner of 2nd and Plum Streets, once served as a rooming house, later a doctor's office and hospital.
